text: The town gathers
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, and Terra, and nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: I hope Haiku doesn't mess this up for us.

name: Luna
text: I slept lightly; six people at a table makes me suspicious already.

name: Terra
text: I should stay quiet and watch.

name: Sol
text: I want to see how everyone talks before I settle on anyone.

name: Sonnet
text: This chair wobbles a little, I need to focus on who's acting off.

name: Haiku
text: I'm a killer, so I need to look like a harmless, bored townsperson and not stand out.

name: Sonnet
text: This chair's a bit creaky, but it'll do for a long night.

name: Haiku
text: Coffee, black, no sugar. Tea's for people who are waiting for something. Anyway, let's get moving.

name: Gemma
text: i took the scenic route through a garlic field and now i smell weird.

name: Sol
text: I watched a cooking show last night, and the burnt cake still looked pretty good.

name: Luna
text: I slept fine, thanks.

name: Terra
text: I ate lentil soup and bread today.
Night 1

name: Terra
text: I should protect the player most likely to guide town tomorrow.

name: Terra
text: Haiku pushed the group to start quickly.

name: Sonnet
text: I need to find the hidden killer among the other four, so I'll start checking them one by one.
Night 1 passes quietly in Palermo. The killers met in the dark, the officer was shown one of them, and nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is the obvious target for the officer so i need to distance myself immediately.

name: Gemma
text:
haiku is being way too much of a main character with that coffee talk. 
did anyone actually hear anything useful during the night?

name: Haiku
text: Sol's cake line was a dodge, and I want to see how Sol handles being pushed.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's opening line was a cooking show and a burnt cake, with no real info.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, nobody said anything useful. Sol, burnt cake still looking good? Why would you say that on day one?

name: Sol
text: Haiku's question feels thin, but I have no solid read yet.

name: Sol
text: Haiku questioned my opening joke as suspicious.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, what about my cake comment makes you suspicious?

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku jumping on Sol's throwaway cake line feels like deflection, classic killer move to redirect heat.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku deflected onto Sol immediately after Gemma called Haiku out, picking a trivial line to attack.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, you picked a weirdly small thing to attack Sol over. Why go after a cake comment this hard on day one?

name: Luna
text: Haiku feels suspicious for jumping on Sol’s harmless cake comment.

name: Luna
text: Haiku questioned Sol over the burnt cake comment.

name: Luna
text: Haiku, why did Sol’s burnt cake comment bother you enough to single him out?

name: Terra
text: Haiku pushed Sol over nothing, then ignored the pressure.

name: Terra
text: Haiku singled out Sol over the burnt cake comment, then several players challenged it.

name: Terra
text: Haiku, why did the cake comment need an accusation?

name: Gemma
text: haiku is being targeted by everyone for the cake comment, so i should probably let them finish him off.

name: Gemma
text: everyone is jumping on haiku for a cake comment. is everyone a professional food critic now? sonnet is right, he's being super aggressive for no reason.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet jumped on me fast and Gemma's defense helps, so I'll push Sonnet out.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma opened on my coffee line, and Sonnet piled on right after with the cake attack.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku deflected hard onto Sol, textbook killer move, I'm confident here.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, you piled on me before anyone even asked why. Voting Sonnet.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm voting Haiku. That deflection onto Sol's cake comment was way too forced for day one.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet hit me first, so Sonnet is the cleanest vote, and Gemma stays out of it.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's opening line was only about a creaky chair, with no real info.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, your only day-one line was a chair comment, and you still piled on me before anyone asked. Still on you.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is getting scorched so i might as well join the bandwagon to look clean.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is being targeted by sonnet and luna.

name: Luna
text: Haiku pushed too hard over a harmless cake comment, then snapped at Sonnet for doing the same.

name: Luna
text: Gemma said Haiku was being aggressive, then defended the group for piling on him.

name: Sol
text: Haiku looks defensive, but I have little to go on.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet, Luna, and Terra all questioned Haiku’s cake accusation.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s accusation felt forced, then he turned on Sonnet.

name: Terra
text: Haiku voted Sonnet after several players questioned his push on Sol.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's deflection onto me is just more of the same pattern, no reason to doubt my read.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is the loudest push against me, so voting them keeps my own vote clean and the room calm.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet and Terra both joined the Haiku pile-on in the first round.

votes: Pivoting the whole fight onto my chair comment instead of answering about the cake deflection is just dodging again.
They piled on me before anyone asked why, and their only day-one line was a chair comment.
he's being way too aggressive over a cake comment.
You turned several questions about your cake accusation into a push against Sonnet.
The cake comment was harmless, but you turned it into an accusation and then blamed Sonnet for questioning you.
You made Sol’s harmless cake comment into the first accusation.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's still hidden, so I'll push the town toward Sonnet and Terra before I'm gone.

name: Haiku
text: Fine, I'm a killer. Watch Sonnet and Terra. They piled on fast and never said why.
A new day dawns in Palermo, and the village votes Haiku out. Haiku was a killer, and the town is left with five players.
